title: CmdPal: App is not being properly disposed

judgment.rationale: The current source confirms a forced process exit after unawaited extension shutdown; this is a precise lifecycle fix with no material uncertainty.
evidence: The issue identifies service disposal and async completion risks.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the app-owned, awaitable shutdown design.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt was found covering the CmdPal shutdown lifecycle issue.

issue_context.summary: CmdPal closes MainWindow by starting asynchronous extension shutdown and then calling Environment.Exit(0). This can bypass service-container disposal and terminate SignalStopAsync work before completion.
known_information: Issue is open and labeled Product-Command Palette.
MainWindow.xaml.cs enumerates IExtensionService and calls SignalStopAsync without awaiting.
It then destroys the tray icon, disposes listeners/backdrop, and calls Environment.Exit(0).
The reporter questions whether async shutdown signals complete.
inferences: Environment.Exit likely prevents normal service disposal and can race extension cleanup.
Shutdown should be owned by App/service lifetime.
issue_context.analysis: The exact sequence is visible in source; replace forced termination with coordinated application shutdown while preserving thread-affine cleanup.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the live cross-reference to #50098 and found no concrete lifecycle fix there.

proposed_fixes.title: Make CmdPal shutdown awaitable and service-owned
proposed_fixes.root_cause: MainWindow_Closed starts async extension stops and force-terminates the process, bypassing normal disposal.
plan: Move shutdown orchestration to App/composition root.
Have MainWindow request shutdown and keep only UI-thread cleanup.
Replace Environment.Exit with supported application exit after services complete.
Add lifecycle tests for disposal and repeated close.
verification: Close with active extensions and verify each stop completes.
Run repeated open/close with FailFast workaround enabled.

confidence.rationale: The forced exit and fire-and-forget calls are confirmed; the lifecycle change is localized and testable.

design.root_cause: MainWindow_Closed is both UI close handler and process lifecycle owner; it calls Environment.Exit immediately after unawaited SignalStopAsync calls.
evidence: The issue identifies disposal and async completion risk.

affected_files.purpose: Current close handler and UI cleanup

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The close handler starts async stops, performs UI cleanup, then force-exits.
implementation_steps.change: Request app shutdown and await/hand off service completion rather than terminating directly.
implementation_steps.code_block:
await App.Current.ShutdownAsync();
// no Environment.Exit from the window close handler

implementation_steps.current_behavior: MainWindow is the effective finish line.
implementation_steps.change: Own one idempotent shutdown task that stops extensions, disposes services, and completes app exit.
implementation_steps.code_block: if (_shutdownTask is null) _shutdownTask = StopExtensionsAsync().ContinueWith(_ => ExitApplication()); await _shutdownTask;

verify: Build CmdPal UI and run focused lifecycle tests.
Close with active extension providers and verify clean termination after stop completion.
risks: Changing shutdown timing can expose thread-affinity assumptions.
Hung extensions need bounded timeout and diagnostics.
alternatives: Keep Environment.Exit and add delays; rejected because disposal is not guaranteed.
Dispose only in MainWindow; rejected because lifecycle remains split.
